modules.name: Energy and carbon limits (HBP s2.2 targets, VBBL Part 10 Tables A/B/C, EMG v3.0, rezoning layer)
modules.design_question: Which TEUI, TEDI and GHGI targets do the Higher Buildings Policy (rezoning) and VBBL 2025 (permit) set for my program mix, does my estimate pass and by what margin, and which rezoning deliverables follow?
inputs: Layer 0: floor area by program tag, mapped to HBP type (residential, hotel, retail, office) and VBBL major occupancy (C, D, E; A, B, F), with user override
Storeys per independent building (tower plus podium count together unless designed as independent structures), user override
Modelled floor area (MFA) per EMG v3.0: excludes indoor parking, includes mechanical and unconditioned space
Regime selector: rezoning (HBP s2.2, default for VTC), permit (VBBL) or both (stricter value per metric); permit-date selector (Jan 2022, Jul 2023, Mar 2025, Sep 2025 wording)
Route selector: Passive House; HBP targets plus LCES (default); VBBL Table A; Table B (Group C only); Table C (LCES attested). Tables B and C are VBBL-only fallbacks
TEUI, TEDI, GHGI from P04-M03 EMG mode (or manual entry); PV deduction from P04-M05 applied to TEUI and GHGI
Reference-model results for 'all other' occupancies and commercial kitchens (manual entry in BASIC mode)
Purchased-renewable flag with lifetime supply guarantee (EMG s1.4.1)
outputs: limits registry rows {TEUI, TEDI, GHGI, regime, effective_date, clause, status, source_id} for HBP and VBBL
MFA-weighted whole-building limits per regime, the stricter-of value, and combined-TEDI and combined-GHGI sub-limits
reference-model GHGI limit for all-other space (0.5 x fossil-only reference)
pass/fail flags and margin (%) per metric, labelled screening
rezoning checklist (HBP route, GBPR deliverables, LCES type, incentive) with status chips
floor-area incentive record for PROG modules
policy-review, by-law 13472 forward-risk and HBP height-guidance flags (cross-packet to SITE and PROG)

parameters.name: Rezoning energy route (HBP s2.2)
parameters.relationship: Higher buildings must achieve Passive House certification, or meet type-specific TEUI/TEDI/GHGI targets and connect to an LCES, with no aggregation of another LCES's reductions. This first choice fixes the target set and makes LCES connection mandatory.

parameters.name: Building type mapping (HBP type, VBBL group)
parameters.relationship: HBP has rows only for residential, hotel, retail and office. Assembly, civic and cultural space (Groups A, B, F) has no HBP row; the VBBL 50%-below-reference GHGI rule is a team-assumed proxy, so more cultural area forces a reference-model run.

parameters.name: Storeys per building (6 or fewer vs over 6)
parameters.relationship: VBBL Group C limits are 110/25 up to 6 storeys and 120/30 above. A tower plus podium classes as one building unless designed as independent structures (10.2.1.1(4)), so every VTC tower is over 6. HBP targets have no storey split.

parameters.name: Compliance path (VBBL fallback)
parameters.relationship: Table B (100/15, GHGI waived) is Group C only. Table C relaxes TEUI/TEDI (office 100 to 130, 20 to 30) only with an LCES; GHGI never relaxes. Under HBP the stricter targets govern, so Table C relief does not apply.

parameters.name: Permit date / table version
parameters.relationship: Residential over 6 storeys GHGI was 6 and hotel 8 (Jul 2023 to Feb 2025); both fell to 3.0 and 4.0 in the 1 Mar 2025 wording. TEUI/TEDI cells did not change. The by-law in force at permit sets the VBBL limit.

parameters.name: Modelled floor area (denominator)
parameters.relationship: Limits and results are per MFA, which excludes indoor parking but includes mechanical and unconditioned space. Parkade energy stays in the numerator, so each parkade level raises TEUI. MFA must be within 5% of drawing GFA or be explained.

parameters.name: Emission factors and on-site renewables
parameters.relationship: GHGI = sum((energy - on-site renewable) x factor) / MFA; electricity 0.011, gas 0.180, district per utility. Gas emits about 16 times more per kWh, so gas-only energy must stay under limit/0.180 (8.3 kWh/m2 at 1.5).

parameters.name: Rezoning policy layer
parameters.relationship: GBPR (amended 27 Nov 2024) requires per building an embodied carbon report and resilience worksheet, plus letters of commitment for enhanced commissioning and sub-metering; no energy modelling. HBP applies on top. SLD adds no energy study.

parameters.name: Floor-area incentive
parameters.relationship: City lists +10% floor space for larger buildings meeting ILFI Zero Energy or Passive House (to 31 Oct 2030), applied through a development or combined permit. Applicability to a CD-1 tower rezoning is unverified; it could fund the Passive House route.

parameters.name: HBP height guidance vs tower height
parameters.relationship: HBP 2.1(c) puts the highest CBD buildings at about 550-700 ft. VTC towers of 244-305 m are about 800-1,000 ft, 14-43% above 700 ft. Height drives stack effect and plant, so the conflict goes to SITE and PROG.

metrics.name: TEUI vs governing weighted limit
metrics.good: <= weighted limit. HBP: residential 100, hotel 120, retail 100, office 100. VBBL Table A (15 Sep 2025): office 100, retail 120, hotel 140, residential over 6 storeys 120. Table C (VBBL-only): 130/170/170/130.
metrics.basis: Corrects 'VBBL Table A sets VTC targets'. HBP (S60) and official VBBL (S62) opened; tables match S42/S49. HBP basis (MFA, EMG) and mixed-use weighting are assumptions; HBP is under review (S37).
metrics.method: L = sum(MFA_i x L_i)/sum(MFA_i) per regime; effective = stricter of HBP and VBBL; margin = (estimate - L)/L; estimate net of on-site PV

metrics.name: TEDI vs governing weighted limit
metrics.good: <= weighted limit. HBP: 15 for all four types. VBBL Table A: office, retail, hotel 20; residential over 6 storeys 30 (6 or fewer 25). Table C: 30/30/30/40. Table B: Group C 15.
metrics.basis: HBP TEDI 15 is stricter than every Table A cell. Corridor adjustment (max 10, min 0) and form adjustment (max 20) are post-processing credits reported before and after (final EMG, S17).
metrics.method: Area-weighted average per regime; add the combined sub-check below

metrics.name: GHGI vs governing weighted limit
metrics.good: <= weighted limit. HBP: residential 3, hotel 4, retail 1.5, office 1.5. VBBL Tables A and C: 3.0 office, retail, Group C; 4.0 hotel (from 1 Mar 2025). Table B waives GHGI. Energy only, net of PV; refrigerants separate.
metrics.basis: HBP retail and office 1.5 is half the VBBL 3.0; residential and hotel equal VBBL. GHGI per EMG Eq. 2 deducts on-site renewable generation (S17).
metrics.method: GHGI = sum((E_fuel - E_renewable) x EF_fuel) / MFA

metrics.name: Gas and electricity headroom under the governing GHGI
metrics.good: Gas-only site energy <= limit/0.180: 8.3 at 1.5, 16.7 at 3.0, 22.2 at 4.0. All-electric site energy <= limit/0.011: 136, 273, 364.
metrics.bad: Gas share above the headroom, or GHGI > limit
metrics.basis: Arithmetic on HBP and VBBL limits with EMG factors 0.180 and 0.011. It shows gas heating is close to excluded for office and retail under HBP.
metrics.method: headroom = limit / emission factor; mixed fuels solve (limit - 0.011 x E_total)/(0.180 - 0.011)

metrics.name: Combined TEDI sub-check (portions with a table TEDI target)
metrics.good: MFA-weighted TEDI of all occupancies with a table TEDI target <= their combined TEDI limit, in addition to the whole-building limit
metrics.bad: Sub-check fails while the whole building passes
metrics.basis: Replaces the residential-only sub-limit. EMG s5.1(e), confirmed in the final text (S17), covers all portions with a TEDI target, excluding reference-model occupancies.
metrics.method: Separate area-weighted TEDI over occupancies with a table target

metrics.name: Combined GHGI sub-check (portions with an absolute GHGI target)
metrics.good: Combined GHGI of those portions <= their combined limit
metrics.bad: Combined GHGI exceeds their combined limit
metrics.basis: EMG s5.1(e), final text opened (S17).
metrics.method: Separate area-weighted GHGI over occupancies with an absolute target

metrics.name: GHGI limit for all-other occupancies (Groups A, B, F) and commercial kitchens
metrics.good: <= 0.5 x GHGI of a fossil-fuel-only reference model (EMG s5.3 shortcut: reference results with gas factor 0.180 for heating, ventilation heating and DHW)
metrics.basis: Official Table A (S62); EMG s5.3 example gives 3.7. Replaces the 2018-20 rule. HBP has no row for these groups (team proxy). Kitchens take reference-model targets (EMG 2.3.4).
metrics.method: GHGI_limit = 0.5 x sum(reference energy x EF) / MFA

metrics.name: GHGI-R (refrigerants), reported only
metrics.good: Report GHGI-R = GWP x charge x (0.02 L + 0.1) / (L x MFA); no VBBL limit
metrics.bad: Counting GHGI-R inside the Table A limit
metrics.basis: Final EMG Eq. 3 (S17) assumes 2% annual and 10% end-of-life leakage and reports it separately. The earlier plan to include it from Jan 2025 was not adopted.
metrics.method: Charge, GWP and service life from P04-M03 inputs

metrics.name: Passive overheating hours (cooling disabled, NRC GW2.0 file)
metrics.good: Report monthly hours above the ASHRAE 55 80% limits (Vancouver: May 25.5, Jun 26.5, Jul 27.5, Aug 28.4, Sep 26.5, Oct 25.2 deg C). 200 h/yr is a team preset; 20 h for vulnerable occupants.
metrics.basis: Final EMG s4 requires reporting and sets no hour limit (defers to the AHJ). The 200 h wording is only in the redline and 2018 EMG. BCBC 2024 adds one cool space at 26 deg C per dwelling.
metrics.method: Hourly zone temperature from P04-M03

metrics.name: HBP height-guidance check
metrics.good: <= about 700 ft (213 m) in the CBD; 550 ft (168 m) or more triggers enhanced review (HBP s3(b))
metrics.bad: > 700 ft: guidance conflict flag for SITE and PROG, no pass/fail
metrics.basis: HBP 2.1(c) uses '~' and 'should'; the policy is under review and the VTC site is hypothetical. Figure 1 (permitted areas) is not text-extractable, so site fit is unverified.
metrics.method: height_m x 3.281 compared with 550 and 700 ft

metrics.name: Forward check: By-law 13472 limits for large existing buildings
metrics.good: 2026: office <= 25, retail <= 14; 2040: GHGI 0 and heat energy intensity <= 0.09 GJ/m2.yr. Lifetime-risk context only.
metrics.bad: Design relies on gas heating that cannot meet the 2040 limit
metrics.basis: 2026 values verified in the Reference Manual (S18) for existing Group D/E buildings of 9,290 m2 or more; 2040 numbers rest on the 2022 deck (S02). A May 2026 motion proposes pausing enforcement (S56).
metrics.method: Compare design GHGI and heat intensity with the schedule

metrics.name: Legacy limit: high-rise residential GHGI 6, hotel GHGI 8
metrics.good: n/a: superseded. Use 3.0 and 4.0 from the 1 Mar 2025 wording; 6 and 8 applied Jul 2023 to Feb 2025.
metrics.bad: Using 6 or 8 for a permit under the 1 Mar 2025 or later wording
metrics.basis: Versioned wordings S05, S43, S42. The earlier 'January 2025' date is corrected to 1 Mar 2025.
metrics.method: Keep visible in the registry in FALSE ASSUMPTION colour

modules.method: 1) Map Layer 0 tags to HBP types and VBBL groups (C, D, E use table rows; A, B, F and kitchens use reference-model rows); derive storey class per building, with override. 2) Compute MFA per EMG v3.0, within 5% of drawing GFA. 3) Look up limits in a versioned JSON registry keyed by regime (HBP, VBBL), permit date and route; each cell carries clause, date, source and status. 4) MFA-weight limits (HBP weighting is a team assumption); effective limit = stricter per metric; add combined sub-checks. 5) Compare estimates (TEUI and GHGI net of PV; GHGI-R separate); margin = (estimate - L)/L. 6) Table C stays locked and is not used under HBP. 7) Show the rezoning checklist, HBP height flag and policy-review banner.
visualization: Three bullet bars (TEUI, TEDI, GHGI): estimate bar, HBP tick and VBBL tick, pass/fail badge linked to the clause
Stacked bar of each occupancy's MFA contribution to the weighted limit, with sub-check ticks
Limits registry table with regime tabs (HBP, VBBL), status chips (verified / team assumption / FALSE ASSUMPTION) and a permit-date slider
Timeline 2021-2040: table steps (Jul 2023, 1 Mar 2025, 15 Sep 2025), HBP amendment 31 Mar 2026, review report-back 2027, by-law 13472 limit 2040
Rezoning-layer checklist card: HBP route, GBPR deliverables, LCES type, incentive, height-guidance flag
modules.human_judgment: Passive House versus targets plus LCES; how City staff classify cultural, civic, amenity and restaurant space; whether a justified breach of HBP targets is worth arguing; LCES type and recognition; confirming values with the City and a qualified energy modeller.
modules.limits: Screening, not compliance: formal compliance needs an EMG v3.0 model by a qualified modeller. HBP basis (MFA, EMG, mixed-use weighting) and Figure 1 areas are unconfirmed. HBP and VBBL are under review (report-back 2027). Passive House criteria and LCES recognition letters unopened.

jury_criteria: cultural_context_30: environmental character, City in Nature

modules.name: Massing energy indicators (VFAR, WWR, orientation, thermal bridging)
modules.design_question: How compact, glazed and oriented is my massing, and what does that imply for heating demand (TEDI) before any simulation is run?
inputs: Layer 0 mesh (faces, normals, storey heights) and program tags (parkade excluded from MFA)
True-north rotation from the site plan (its north arrow is rotated from the street grid)
WWR per facade (default preset or imported glazing)
EPW weather file for heating degree days (NRC GW1.0 for EMG-consistent proxy; TMYx optional)
Slab-edge, balcony and spandrel details: psi (W/m.K) x length per storey and effective-U presets (BETBG-style); balcony length shared with P04-M07
Target whole-building airtightness (L/s.m2 at 75 Pa)
Optional: U-value and heat-recovery presets from ADVANCED mode
outputs: indicator set {VFAR, envelope/volume, perimeter/GFA, plate depth, WWR and glazed area by azimuth}
per-storey table
facade-area-by-azimuth grid
TEDI_proxy band (kWh/m2.yr) with calibration status
EMG form-adjustment eligibility flag
perimeter/core zoning and effective-U inputs for P04-M03
glazing areas for CLIM and SPAC modules

parameters.name: Vertical facade area / floor area (VFAR)
parameters.relationship: EMG v3.0: VFAR = above-ground wall area / MFA; higher VFAR raises TEDI. At 0.65 or more, a site-forced slim form may subtract 40 x (VFAR - 0.65), max 20, times (2 - 3000/HDD). Towers are expected below 0.65; the tool calculates it.

parameters.name: Window-to-wall ratio
parameters.relationship: Higher WWR raises glazing heat loss (TEDI), solar gain and daylight. The VBBL NECB path caps reference-building WWR at 40% and vertical SHGC at 0.36, so glazing beyond 40% earns no allowance in reference-model comparisons.

parameters.name: Thermal bridging at slab edges, balconies and spandrels
parameters.unit: psi (W/m.K) x m per storey; effective U (W/m2K)
parameters.relationship: EMG v3.0 requires interface-detail heat loss inside effective U-values (BETBG method). Balcony slabs, cladding attachments and window-wall slab by-pass were historically underestimated, so clear-field U understates TEDI; thermal breaks and balcony removal change TEDI directly.

parameters.name: Facade azimuth relative to true north
parameters.relationship: Azimuth sets solar gain and glare per m2 of glass. The site plan's north arrow is rotated from the street grid, so grid north would misassign exposure. Size of the effect for Vancouver towers is unsourced.

parameters.name: Floor-plate depth (facade to core)
parameters.relationship: Deeper plates lower envelope per m2 of floor (TEDI down) but cut daylight and natural-ventilation reach. Effect on glazing need and cooling is unsourced and left to P04-M03.

parameters.name: Tower height / slenderness
parameters.relationship: Greater height strengthens stack effect and wind pressure, raising infiltration and corridor-pressurization loads. Final EMG keeps the corridor TEDI/TEUI adjustment at max 10 (min 0; Focal's 5 was not adopted). Height magnitude is unsourced.

parameters.name: Airtightness target
parameters.relationship: EMG v3.0 converts targeted leakage to modelled infiltration (x 0.112 on above-ground wall area). 1.5 is the suggested start, 1.0 very good, 0.70 exceptional; below 1.30 needs a sealed narrative. Tighter targets cut TEDI.

metrics.name: Vertical facade-to-floor ratio (VFAR, EMG definition)
metrics.good: Report only; informational line at 0.65 (form-adjustment eligibility, not a pass line)
metrics.bad: VFAR >= 0.65 without site-forced slimness: adjustment not claimable
metrics.basis: Final EMG s2.7 (S17): eligibility needs site-forced slimness; adjustment capped at 20.
metrics.method: Above-ground wall area / MFA by storey

metrics.name: Envelope-to-floor ratio vs reference box
metrics.good: At or below a reference box of equal GFA and height (relative comparison)
metrics.bad: Above the reference box by more than a user-set tolerance
metrics.basis: No City or code threshold found for towers; a relative comparison avoids inventing an absolute number. Engineering reasoning, not a sourced relationship.
metrics.method: Ratio of design to reference-box value

metrics.name: Whole-building and per-azimuth WWR
metrics.good: <= 40% (reference-building cap, VBBL 10.2.2.3)
metrics.basis: 40% is the sourced NECB-path reference cap (S62); using it as a design target is a team choice. The eSim 57% to 40% case is an example only.
metrics.method: Glazed area / gross wall area by storey and sector

metrics.name: TEDI proxy band vs P04-M01 TEDI limit
metrics.good: Band upper bound <= governing TEDI limit (HBP 15; Table A 20-30; Table C 30-40); pass badge greyed until calibrated
metrics.bad: Band lower bound > governing TEDI limit
metrics.basis: Steady-state proxy is unvalidated; high-gain offices have low balance points. Calibrate per occupancy against P04-M03 runs and show a band, not a point.
metrics.method: Effective UA x HDD plus ventilation and infiltration loss less usable gains, / MFA

metrics.name: Glazing share facing south-west to west
metrics.good: No sourced threshold
metrics.basis: Orientation effect for Vancouver towers not sourced; show as information only.
metrics.method: Glazed area in 202.5-292.5 degree sectors / total glazed area

metrics.name: Effective-to-clear-field U ratio
metrics.good: No sourced threshold: report the ratio
metrics.basis: EMG s3 requires bridged U-values; BETBG psi presets not opened, so presets are team assumptions.
metrics.method: U_effective / U_clear-field by assembly

modules.method: 1) Slice the mesh per storey; classify exterior faces by normal tilt (default 10 degrees) into walls and roof. 2) Rotate normals by the true-north offset and bin into 8 azimuth sectors. 3) MFA = tagged floor area (parkade excluded); VFAR = above-ground wall area / MFA; plate depth = longest facade-to-core distance. 4) Glazing = WWR preset x wall area. 5) Effective U = clear-field U plus psi x length bridging per storey (BETBG-style presets, team assumption). 6) TEDI proxy band = [UA_eff x HDD x 24/1000 + ventilation loss x (1 - SRE) + infiltration loss - usable gains] / MFA, HDD from the EPW; show a range from preset bands; recalibrate against P04-M03. 7) Compare indicators with an equal-GFA reference box; flag VFAR >= 0.65.
visualization: Polar bar chart (8 sectors) of glazed area by solar-exposure class, with true-north and street-grid-north ticks
Radar chart of normalised indicators, design vs reference box
Per-storey line chart (WWR, VFAR, plate depth) beside the 3D massing coloured by facade orientation
Bullet band of the TEDI proxy against the P04-M01 limit with a greyed-until-calibrated badge
modules.human_judgment: Facade composition, glazing versus views, daylight and cultural expression; whether higher WWR is justified by human-scale and City in Nature intent; shading, fin and balcony strategy.
modules.limits: Screening proxy only: no thermal mass, HVAC or stack model. Bridging presets, orientation and plate-depth magnitudes are unsourced. Relative indicators depend on the reference box. Not a compliance calculation.

modules.name: Shoebox energy model: TEUI, TEDI, GHGI and peak loads (EMG mode and Physics mode)
modules.design_question: What TEUI, TEDI, GHGI, peak loads and end-use split do my program and envelope produce, using a transparent sample-storey EnergyPlus model that follows the City guidelines?
inputs: Layer 0 geometry and program tags; MFA per EMG
P04-M02 zoning (perimeter/core), WWR, effective U-values and glazing by azimuth
ADVANCED presets: air-tightness target, heat-recovery SRE and frost control, lighting/plug densities, HVAC type and COP, schedules
Refrigerant type (GWP), charge per kW, service life
DHW demand by occupancy and DHW plant/source
Elevator count, parkade fan and lighting loads, commercial kitchen areas
P04-M06 supply option and emission factors
Weather: NRC GW1.0 (EMG mode), GW2.0 (overheating), TMYx or future files (Physics mode)
outputs: Annual end uses by fuel (kWh/yr)
TEUI, TEDI, GHGI, CEDI and GHGI-R by occupancy and whole building, pre- and post-adjustment
Peak heating and cooling loads (W/m2)
Hourly electric and thermal load profiles (8760) for P04-M04, M05, M06
Passive overheating hours per zone

parameters.name: Opaque and glazing effective U-values
parameters.relationship: Lower effective U cuts conductive loss and TEDI; EMG requires bridged U-values. City baselines use double-pane window wall (S02, S64), so glazing upgrades trade TEDI against enclosure embodied carbon (P04-M07).

parameters.name: Heat-recovery sensible effectiveness and frost control
parameters.relationship: Higher SRE cuts ventilation heating, a large TEDI part. EMG requires SRE with fan-heat treatment and an electric preheat coil if no frost control is specified, so unrealistic recovery is not rewarded.

parameters.name: Airtightness target and modelled infiltration
parameters.relationship: EMG v3.0 models infiltration from targeted leakage (x 0.112 on above-ground wall area). Leakage below 1.30 needs a sealed narrative. Lower leakage cuts TEDI; fixed height multipliers are not part of EMG mode.

parameters.name: Domestic hot water demand and plant
parameters.relationship: DHW is outside TEDI but inside TEUI and GHGI. EMG sets 0.0016 L/s per person peak, 5 deg C inlet, drain-heat recovery up to 15%. Gas DHW alone must stay under limit/0.180: 16.7 kWh/m2 at 3.0, 8.3 at 1.5.

parameters.name: Refrigerant type, charge and leakage (GHGI-R)
parameters.relationship: EMG: GHGI-R = GWP x charge x (0.02 L + 0.1) / (L x MFA), reported with no limit. City-study archetypes: central heat pumps 0.2-0.9, 3-pipe VRF 1.7-2.6 kgCO2e/m2.yr, so system type is a carbon decision.

parameters.name: Plant type and efficiency
parameters.relationship: TEDI is independent of plant; TEUI falls with COP. Emission factors are fixed (electricity 0.011, gas 0.180, district per utility), so replacing gas with electricity cuts GHGI about 16-fold per kWh.

parameters.name: Dwelling cooling provision
parameters.relationship: BCBC 2024 (in VBBL 2025) requires one cool space at or below 26 deg C per dwelling. Cooling adds to TEUI and is reported as CEDI, which has no VBBL limit; passively cooled designs previously excluded it.

parameters.name: Vertical transportation
parameters.relationship: EMG models each elevator at 3 kW on the building schedule; the City flagged elevator methodology for future review. Car count from SYST therefore moves TEUI in a 244-305 m tower.

parameters.name: Parkade lighting, fans and heating
parameters.relationship: Parkade lighting (24 h), fans (4 h/day) and heating above a 7 deg C setpoint are site energy, but parking area is outside MFA, so each parkade level raises per-m2 results. This links MOBI parking to energy.

parameters.name: Pool and amenity programme
parameters.relationship: Pool-water heating counts in TEUI and GHGI but is excluded from TEDI under EMG v3.0; pool-hall conditioning and ventilation heating still count in TEDI. A 2018 case had 58% of heating from pools.

parameters.name: Commercial kitchens and restaurants
parameters.relationship: EMG treats a commercial kitchen as a pseudo major occupancy whose targets come from a reference model, so restaurant area adds reference-model work and sits outside the table rows.

parameters.name: Lighting, plug loads and schedules
parameters.relationship: Suite plug load 5 W/m2 (gas cooking splits 1 gas, 4 electric), suite lighting per design up to 5 W/m2, schedules per NECB 2020. Higher gains cut TEDI but raise TEUI and cooling.

parameters.name: Weather file
parameters.relationship: EMG mode uses the NRC GW1.0 future-shifted TMY (energy) and GW2.0 (overheating), linked in EMG s1.5; Physics mode may use TMYx or future files. Results compare with limits only in EMG mode.

metrics.name: Modelled TEUI, TEDI, GHGI (EMG mode) vs P04-M01 limits
metrics.good: <= governing MFA-weighted limits from P04-M01 (and combined sub-limits)
metrics.basis: Limits verified (S60, S62). The model is a screening estimate; Physics mode shows no pass/fail. Adjustments are reported pre and post.
metrics.method: EnergyPlus annual results by end use and fuel, with EMG inputs and post-processing adjustments reported pre and post

metrics.name: Passive overheating hours (cooling disabled, GW2.0)
metrics.good: Report monthly hours; 200 h/yr team preset for non-mechanically-cooled spaces; 20 h for vulnerable occupants
metrics.basis: Final EMG s4 sets no hour limit and defers to the AHJ; the 200 h value comes from the 2018 EMG via a 2020 paper and the redline. Monthly acceptability limits are verified (S17).
metrics.method: Hours above the ASHRAE 55 80% limit per zone, cooling disabled

metrics.name: Cooling energy demand intensity (CEDI)
metrics.good: Report only; VBBL has no CEDI limit
metrics.basis: City 2026 study states CEDI is reporting-only; EMG v3.0 defines it (S17).
metrics.method: Annual cooling output per MFA

metrics.name: Peak heating and cooling load density
metrics.good: No sourced threshold
metrics.basis: Reported for sizing and for P04-M04/M06 only. City study archetypes: 27-48 W/m2 (residential, not towers).
metrics.method: Design-day peaks from the model

modules.method: Two modes. EMG mode (the only mode compared with P04-M01): sample-storey Honeybee/OpenStudio models per height band (perimeter depth from P04-M02, core zone) with EMG inputs: NRC GW1.0 weather, NECB 2020 schedules, suite gains and DHW, elevators 3 kW, infiltration from target leakage (x 0.112), effective U, SRE-based HRV, factors 0.011 and 0.180 (district per utility). Scale by storey count; add podium, retail, amenity, kitchen, parkade and plant zones. Apply corridor and form adjustments as post-processing; report pre and post. TEDI = space and ventilation heating before plant efficiency; GHGI = sum((fuel - renewable) x EF)/MFA; GHGI-R and CEDI separate. Physics mode (exploratory, no pass/fail): TMYx or future files, stack/wind multipliers, 8760 export. Fast mode: labelled surrogate over presets.
visualization: Sankey diagram of end uses by fuel
Monthly stacked bars of heating, cooling, lighting, plant
Heat-balance waterfall (losses and gains per m2)
Parallel-coordinates plot of design options with limit bands (EMG mode only)
8760 false-colour heatmap of electric load (day vs hour, kW legend)
modules.human_judgment: Selecting archetype assumptions, plant and refrigerant strategy, schedules and acceptable overheating; interpreting results against policy; deciding when a qualified modeller must replace the screening model.
modules.limits: Sample floors miss podium-tower coupling and detailed plant. Final EMG v3.0 read; NRC file licence not checked. Not compliance-grade. Physics-mode multipliers are unsourced; surrogate accuracy untested.

parameters.name: Demand density by use (electrified-load presets)
parameters.relationship: Peak scales with area times density. No Vancouver-sourced values were found, so presets (heat pump at design-day COP, unit cooling, EV) are labelled team assumptions until a utility or engineer supplies values.

parameters.name: Heating electrification (heat-pump COP, backup)
parameters.relationship: Electric heat moves load to cold winter evenings. A City study found service sizing follows the larger of heating or cooling load in efficient buildings. District steam moves the peak upstream.

parameters.name: Cooling electrification
parameters.relationship: BCBC 2024 requires one cool space per dwelling, adding a summer coincident peak that heat-pump heating does not offset. It sets service size when cooling load exceeds heating load.

parameters.name: Coincidence / diversity factor
parameters.relationship: Total peak is below the sum of use-wise peaks. The Canadian Electrical Code accepts a 'demonstrated load' (24 months of measured W/m2) in place of calculated load when a qualified person does the calculation.

parameters.name: EV charging stalls and kW per stall
parameters.relationship: Each stall adds charger kW to the coincident peak unless managed. EMG excludes EV charging from building loads, so it moves peak, not TEUI. VBBL 10.3.1.1(2) lets the CBO set minimum EV energy-management performance.

parameters.name: Thermal storage / load shedding
parameters.relationship: Storage shifts heating or cooling electricity out of the peak and lowers kVA, at the cost of plant space. HBP encourages innovative peak-load management; effect size is project-specific.

metrics.name: Peak demand vs confirmed service allocation
metrics.good: <= allocation confirmed by BC Hydro (user input)
metrics.basis: No public allocation rule found; downtown context: Dal Grauer replaced by West End substation (as early as 2032), Murrin by East Vancouver (as early as 2031). City staff say the CBO can make allowances if BC Hydro cannot serve.
metrics.method: Peak of aggregated hourly load / power factor

metrics.name: Demand density vs reference ranges
metrics.good: Within user-selected reference range
metrics.basis: CE Code Table 14 office basic load of about 50 W/m2 (lighting and receptacles only) is quoted by a forum post and not confirmed; McFadyen's tables unopened.
metrics.method: Peak kW / GFA by use

metrics.name: Multi-unit residential planning demand (Toronto Hydro, context only)
metrics.good: No pass/fail. Context: class average under 200 units 166; 200-500 units 410; over 500 units 903
metrics.basis: Toronto planning values (Sept 2025), end uses not stated; an all-electric Vancouver supertall with cooling will exceed them by design, so transfer is unverified.
metrics.method: Show beside the residential block peak as a reference line only

metrics.name: Winter-peak share of annual peak
metrics.good: No sourced threshold
metrics.basis: Information only; Creative Energy says it is considering how its systems can ease winter peaks.
metrics.method: Share of top-1% hours falling in Dec-Feb

modules.method: Two modes. Preset mode: peak_i = A_i x density_i (electrified-load presets, editable, team assumption) x coincidence factor; sum; add EV (with optional load-management factor), vertical transport, cooling and plant; kVA = kW / power factor. Profile mode: take hourly electric loads from P04-M03, add heat-pump or electrode-boiler electricity from P04-M06 and EV schedules, aggregate to 8760 hours, then find peak, load factor, winter and summer shares and the load-duration curve. Compare with the user-entered service allocation. A context card cites BC Hydro's substation replacements, VBBL 10.3.1.1 (service capacity per the Electrical Safety Regulation), Electrical By-law 5563 (CE Code Part I) and tells the user to confirm interim capacity with BC Hydro.
visualization: 8760 heatmap (day vs hour) with a kW colour legend
Load-duration curve with the confirmed service allocation as a horizontal line
Stacked bars of coincident peak by use
Grid-context card linking the BC Hydro, provincial and City by-law sources
modules.human_judgment: Negotiation with BC Hydro, service voltage and redundancy, diversity factors and demonstrated-load claims by an electrical engineer, backup generation and storage choices.
modules.limits: Densities are team presets; profile mode inherits all P04-M03 limits. No public BC Hydro capacity figure for the site. City Electrical By-law 5563 opened: it adopts CE Code Part I and sets no capacity rule; BC Hydro's large-load process unopened. The VTC site is hypothetical.

modules.name: On-site PV potential (roof and facade), its TEUI and GHGI credit, and carbon payback
modules.design_question: How much electricity can roof and facade PV realistically supply on a shaded supertall, how much TEUI and GHGI does it remove, what is its carbon payback, and where is PV worth installing?
inputs: Layer 0 roof planes and facade faces with normals
Context massing (existing and approved towers) from SITE modules for shading
Weather file (EPW, dataset reported)
Usable-area fractions (mechanical, terraces, setbacks, green roof)
P04-M03 hourly electric demand and MFA
Module efficiency and loss presets
PV embodied carbon per kWp (EPD value or team assumption)
outputs: PV area and kWp by surface class
Annual and hourly PV generation
Specific yield (kWh/kWp.yr) by surface class
PV share of annual and midday demand

Irradiance map for CLIM and PRES modules

parameters.name: TEUI and GHGI credit under EMG
parameters.relationship: EMG Eq. 2 and Eq. 5 subtract on-site renewable generation from site energy before applying the factor, so PV lowers TEUI directly and GHGI at 0.011. The credit is small because the electricity factor is low.

parameters.name: Usable roof fraction
parameters.relationship: Mechanical plant, amenity terraces and setbacks reduce PV area. SLD A.3.2 asks non-accessible roofs for extensive green roof alongside solar panels, so roof area is shared with vegetation. A supertall roof is small relative to floor area.

parameters.name: Surface tilt and azimuth
parameters.relationship: IEA PVPS Task 12 gives Canadian averages of 1,173 kWh/kWp.yr for rooftop and 821 for facade (about 70%). pvlib computes plane-of-array irradiance for any tilt and azimuth, so the Vancouver ranking is calculated.

parameters.name: Shading from context towers
parameters.relationship: Neighbouring 244-305 m towers shade lower facades and sometimes roofs; loss is computed hourly by ray casting from the context massing.

parameters.name: Weather dataset
parameters.relationship: The 2026 TMYx release takes solar radiation from ERA5, so yield differs from older files; EMG compliance runs use the NRC GW1.0 file. Report the dataset used and keep PV and demand on the same file.

parameters.name: Module efficiency and system losses
parameters.relationship: Higher efficiency raises kWp per m2 of surface; temperature, soiling and inverter losses scale output. Defaults are editable presets, not sourced values.

parameters.name: Demand profile
parameters.relationship: PV fraction falls as tower demand rises relative to roof area. Midday office loads coincide with PV; winter evening heating and residential loads do not.

parameters.name: PV embodied carbon and carbon payback
parameters.relationship: Modules, mounting, inverter replacement and end of life carry embodied carbon, entered from EPDs (IEA PVPS 2020 gives inventories, not results). On BC's low-carbon grid, shaded facade PV may pay back slowly, so rank surfaces by net carbon.

metrics.name: Annual PV generation and specific yield
metrics.good: No sourced Vancouver threshold: report values and rank surfaces. Country-average reference (Canada): rooftop 1,173, facade 821 kWh/kWp.yr
metrics.basis: IEA PVPS Table 3 gives Canadian averages, not Vancouver; no Vancouver benchmark opened; NRCan PV maps were not reachable.
metrics.method: pvlib transposition plus PVWatts-type chain on hourly EPW

metrics.name: TEUI credit from PV (deduction in M01)
metrics.good: Report deduction = PV kWh / MFA; no cap found in the EMG definition
metrics.bad: No threshold; a deduction that is not sited and sized in the design is not claimable
metrics.basis: Final EMG TEUI definition and Eq. 5 (S17); cap, metering and the Roof Mounted Energy bulletin unopened.
metrics.method: Annual PV kWh consumed or exported / MFA

metrics.name: GHGI credit from PV (deduction in M01)
metrics.good: Report deduction = PV kWh x 0.011 / MFA
metrics.bad: Claiming no GHGI effect, or a deduction larger than electricity use
metrics.basis: Corrects 'GHGI treatment unresolved': final EMG Eq. 2 subtracts site renewable generation before the factor (S17). The 7% rule in v2.0 sat in a deleted section.
metrics.method: GHGI deduction = annual PV kWh x EF_electricity / MFA

metrics.name: PV carbon payback by surface class
metrics.good: Payback = EC_PV / (yield x displaced factor) below module service life and a user-set cut-off (team assumption)
metrics.bad: Payback above the cut-off or service life
metrics.basis: Arithmetic: each 100 kgCO2e/kWp pays back in 7.8 yr on roof (1,173 kWh/kWp) and 11.1 yr on facade (821) at 0.011, or 3.7 and 5.3 yr at 0.0228. EC_PV itself is unsourced.
metrics.method: EC_PV (kgCO2e/kWp) / (specific yield x grid factor), at the EMG and BC 2025 factors

metrics.name: PV share of annual electricity use
metrics.good: User-set target (no sourced target; no code requirement for on-site renewables found)
metrics.basis: No VBBL requirement for on-site generation found in Part 10 text (S42, S62).
metrics.method: Annual PV kWh / annual electricity kWh from P04-M03

metrics.name: Surface ranking by yield and net carbon
metrics.good: Top-ranked surfaces by computed yield and by net carbon after embodied debit
metrics.bad: Surfaces below the cut-off the user sets
metrics.basis: Cut-off is a user preset; no sourced viability threshold.
metrics.method: Sort surfaces by annual irradiance after shading, then by net carbon

modules.method: 1) Extract roof planes and facade faces from Layer 0; apply usable-fraction presets (green roof share per SLD A.3.2). 2) Read EPW irradiance. 3) For each surface compute plane-of-array irradiance with pvlib, with hourly shading from context massing by ray casting. 4) Convert to AC output with a PVWatts-type model using editable efficiency, temperature coefficient and loss presets. 5) Sum by surface class; compare with hourly demand from P04-M03 for annual and midday PV fraction, self-consumption and export. 6) Rank surfaces by yield and by net carbon (embodied debit, payback). 7) Show PV share next to total tower demand. 8) Pass annual kWh / MFA to P04-M01 as TEUI deduction and kWh x 0.011 / MFA as GHGI deduction, shown separately.
visualization: False-colour irradiance map on roof and facade meshes (kWh/m2.yr legend) with PV-suitable surfaces outlined
Monthly bars of PV generation vs demand
Ranked bar chart of specific yield and carbon payback by surface class
Hourly overlay of PV and demand for a winter and a summer week
TEUI and GHGI bars with PV deduction shown as a separate segment
modules.human_judgment: Whether PV is architecturally acceptable on facades or the crown, BIPV aesthetics, structural and maintenance access, and whether on-site generation is worth the carbon and cost.
modules.limits: Yield depends on weather dataset and context-shading quality; no verified Vancouver benchmark. Facade PV economics, wind loads and glare not covered. Any cap on the TEUI credit is unverified. PV embodied carbon values are user inputs. Loss and efficiency defaults are presets.

modules.name: LCES connection (required under HBP) and district energy options
modules.design_question: Which low-carbon energy system (LCES) type can the tower use to satisfy the Higher Buildings Policy, what does each type demand, and what does it do to GHGI and electrical peak?
inputs: P04-M03 heating, hot-water and cooling energy and peak loads
Supply option selector (all-electric heat pump, district steam or hot water, hybrid, gas with purchased renewable)
LCES type selector (1, 2a, 2b, 3, 4) with type-specific evidence fields
Type 3 inputs: seasonal average COP, modelled GHGI, gas peaking size, 2-year and 5-year contract references
Utility-confirmed district emission factor and efficiency (user entry); Energy Reporting Agreement status
Site location (Layer 0 / SITE modules)
outputs: Option comparison {TEUI, TEDI, GHGI, electric peak}
LCES type checklist with passed and open items and a building-permit gate flag
Governing route for P04-M01 (HBP targets; Table C only in VBBL-only mode)
District-supply emission factor record
Heat-density and service-availability flags
Evidence list for the Energy Reporting Agreement and the chosen LCES type

parameters.name: LCES requirement under HBP
parameters.relationship: HBP route (b) makes LCES connection mandatory and bars aggregating another LCES's reductions; its stricter targets replace Table C relief. A design with no LCES must instead reach Passive House, which changes plant and envelope strategy.

parameters.name: LCES Type 3 (user-owned on-site) criteria
parameters.relationship: Needs seasonal average COP above 2, modelled GHGI below limit minus 33%, gas peaking sized only to augment, and 2-year and 5-year contracts. At HBP office GHGI 1.5 that means below 1.005, about 91 kWh/m2 all-electric.

parameters.name: LCES Type 4 (existing utility district system, e.g. Creative Energy)
parameters.relationship: Needs interim low-carbon supply, a feasibility study and business plan, progress evidence, a binding City agreement, a title covenant and annual reporting; the City may close this route. Reliance on district steam depends on these.

parameters.name: LCES Types 1, 2a and 2b (City- or utility-owned)
parameters.relationship: Type 2a needs an engineer's verification and a utility purchase; Type 2b needs a feasibility study, a BCUC certificate, supply evidence and annual reporting. No Type 2b existed in 2017. These set who owns the plant.

parameters.name: Building-permit gate and Energy Reporting Agreement
parameters.relationship: No building permit application until the chosen type's requirements are met; every LCES pathway needs an Energy Reporting Agreement for annual metered reporting. This pulls utility talks into schematic design.

parameters.name: District emission factor
parameters.relationship: The factor is set per project by the utility and the AHJ; no steam factor was found. EMG lets heat be modelled as delivered at 100% efficiency or the whole district system be included at the agreed efficiency.

parameters.name: Connection availability
parameters.relationship: Downtown has no forced-connection by-law; the utility expands opportunistically, so a tower must confirm availability. The plant was announced for roughly 12 million ft2 of new development shared among projects (2021, status unverified).

parameters.name: Heating peak density
parameters.relationship: A higher heating peak needs more steam or hot-water capacity from a finite plant and, if all-electric, a larger electric winter peak (P04-M04).

parameters.name: Purchased renewable energy (RNG) path
parameters.relationship: EMG s1.4.1 allows factor zero for the renewable portion if lifetime supply guarantees satisfy the AHJ. It could keep gas peaking within GHGI limits; whether it satisfies HBP or LCES is unverified, and an accounting zero is not physical zero.

metrics.name: Type 3 LCES test (COP and GHGI margin)
metrics.good: COP > 2 and modelled GHGI < 0.67 x governing limit (HBP: residential < 2.01, hotel < 2.68, retail and office < 1.005)
metrics.basis: Corrects 'heat pump as LCES unresolved': LCES Policy s7 defines Type 3 (S41). Applying it to the HBP limit is a team interpretation; a heat pump is not automatically an LCES.
metrics.method: GHGI_model / limit <= 0.67 and seasonal COP > 2

metrics.name: Limit relief when LCES-attested (Table C minus Table A), VBBL-only mode
metrics.good: LCES attested with document and GHGI <= limit
metrics.bad: Relies on TEUI/TEDI relief without attestation, or GHGI > limit
metrics.basis: Table values verified (S62, S42, S49): office +30/+10, retail +50/+10, hotel +30/+10, residential over 6 +10/+10. Not applicable under HBP, whose targets are stricter.
metrics.method: Difference of table cells per occupancy; applied only after attestation

metrics.name: GHGI by supply option
metrics.good: <= P04-M01 governing GHGI limit
metrics.basis: Limit from P04-M01; electricity 0.011 and gas 0.180 verified in EMG (S17); district factor is a user entry, unsourced.
metrics.method: Delivered energy x factor per option / MFA

metrics.name: GHGI with purchased renewable (compliance) vs physical factor
metrics.good: Report both: compliance GHGI with zero factor on the guaranteed portion, and GHGI at the physical factor
metrics.basis: Rule verified in EMG s1.4.1 (S17); LCA caveat is team reasoning and the HBP/LCES status of RNG is unverified.
metrics.method: Split gas into guaranteed renewable and fossil portions

metrics.name: Plant capacity headroom
metrics.unit: MW or m2 of new development
metrics.good: Project demand within capacity the utility confirms
metrics.basis: The 12 million ft2 figure is from 2021 announcements; the City letter gives at least 10 MW; 2026 commissioning status was not found.
metrics.method: User-entered utility letter value vs project load

modules.method: 1) Take annual heating, hot-water and cooling energy and peaks from P04-M03. 2) For each supply option (A all-electric heat pump, B district steam or hot water, C hybrid with heat recovery and peaking, D gas plus purchased renewable) compute delivered energy by fuel with editable efficiencies; electricity 0.011, gas 0.180, district factor from the utility. 3) Re-evaluate TEUI, TEDI and GHGI against the governing limit from P04-M01. 4) Run the LCES type checklist (Types 1-4) and the Type 3 test; flag the permit gate and Energy Reporting Agreement. 5) Compute the added electric peak (heat pump at design-day COP vs upstream electrode boiler). 6) Table C unlocks only in VBBL-only mode after attestation. 7) Output the comparison with source badges.
visualization: Three option cards (A, B, C) with GHGI bars against the HBP and VBBL limit ticks and an LCES-type badge
LCES Type 1-4 checklist card with open items and permit-gate flag
Sankey of heat sources to end uses for the selected option
Bar pair showing winter electric peak with and without district supply
Site pin against a service-area polygon when the user uploads one
modules.human_judgment: Negotiating connection and tariff with the utility, obtaining the City's LCES recognition, accepting dependence on a district plant, whether heat-pump systems or district steam better fit the project, and whether RNG is credible.
modules.limits: The LCES Policy dates from 2017; Type 4 status, Creative Energy's 2026 plant status, capacity and factor are unverified. Recognition is the City's decision. District factors are user inputs. The Energy Reporting Policy is unopened. The site is hypothetical.

modules.name: Embodied carbon at massing stage (VBBL 10.4, National wbLCA Guide + City Addendum, GBPR on-track test)
modules.design_question: Will the tower's embodied carbon meet today's limit (2 x benchmark) and look on track for the limits expected at its first building permit, and which structure and envelope choices move it most?
inputs: Layer 0 GFA_NRC (fully enclosed area to outside wall face, excluding attached garages), storeys above and below grade, one record per building
Structural system preset from STRC (concrete core with flat slab, steel composite, mass-timber hybrid), spans and concrete strength by height band
Envelope type and glazing from P04-M02/M03; balcony and canopy area or length shared with M02
Parkade levels and stalls from MOBI; user choice on whether the below-grade transit link is in the object of assessment
User-typed material carbon factors or EPD values (Reported GWP), with the user's own licence attestation
Selectors: path (intensity or baseline), permit date, expected first Building Permit date (default 2028 or later, team assumption)
Optional retained existing structure (m2, material)
outputs: EC intensity range (kgCO2e/m2 GFA_NRC) and total (tCO2e) by element (substructure, shell) and stage A1-C4, per building
Headline ratio intensity / 400 benchmark against limit 2.0 (to 2.05 with ILC); baseline-path ratio shown as non-binding
Regime badges: current by-law f = 2 and expected-at-BP risk lines (amber, sourced)
Lever ranking (what-if deltas) for STRC and SPAC
Embodied Carbon Design Report draft fields, one report per building and per parcel

parameters.name: Compliance path (intensity vs baseline)
parameters.relationship: Intensity limit is 2 x 400 = 800 kgCO2e/m2 GFA, independent of parkade area. The baseline path drops parking, height, soil and shape variables, but at massing stage a design equals its own baseline, so intensity is the binding test.

parameters.name: Expected first Building Permit date
parameters.relationship: GBPR requires the rezoning report to show the project is on track for limits expected at its first Building Permit. A tower reaching permit in 2028 or later may face the delayed 2025 proposal or later steps, so f = 2 may not bind.

parameters.name: Structural system and material intensity
parameters.relationship: Structure and substructure dominate upfront carbon. MH 2023 gives 97-424 kgCO2e/m2 (median 260, baseline 311) for a 30-storey residential archetype. Presets are team assumptions with ranges; S59 is kept for lever ratios only.

parameters.name: Height premium above 40 storeys
parameters.relationship: Taller towers need larger columns, outriggers and foundations, and encapsulated mass timber stops at 18 storeys, so a supertall is a hybrid. MH 2023 corrected column quantities from 30-37 storey designs; no 244-305 m benchmark was opened. Use a wide band.

parameters.name: Concrete SCM content and strength
parameters.relationship: MH 2023: 0 to 20% SCM cuts element GWP 3.6-5.2%, 0 to 30% cuts 10.4-12.2%, 0 to 40% cuts 15.5-20.1%; its baseline is 20% SCM. NRC defaults 25/35/40 MPa apply only without design data, so map strength by height.

parameters.name: Below-grade parking levels and baseline defaults
parameters.relationship: Parkade structure counts in the assessed object but its area is outside GFA, so each level raises kg/m2. Baseline parking (path B only) uses Addendum defaults: office tower 54.73 m2/space, office plus retail 52.23, 12+ storey apartment 0.98 strata or 0.54 rental spaces/unit.

parameters.name: Groundwater rule and basement depth
parameters.relationship: SLD E.3.1 bars permanent groundwater discharge to sewers, so a parkade below the yearly high water table must be tanked, which may add concrete. Size of the effect is unsourced; link to MOBI and STRC.

parameters.name: Facade system and glazing
parameters.relationship: MH 2023 baseline is aluminum window wall, 40% WWR, double glazing. In S59, steel-stud double-glazed walls cut 11% against curtain wall and triple glazing added 2%. Read P04-M02/M03 and M07 together.

parameters.name: Balconies, canopies and stairs
parameters.relationship: The NRC required scope includes balconies, canopies, stairs and below-grade floors. Balconies are also a thermal-bridge lever (M02), so one balcony decision moves both TEDI and embodied carbon.

parameters.name: Product-specific EPDs and procurement
parameters.relationship: A design with manufacturer EPDs against an industry-average baseline widens the reduction. Reported GWP must be used, not uncertainty-adjusted GWP, and the same tool for both.

parameters.name: Missing life-cycle stage placeholders
parameters.relationship: Only when a tool lacks a whole stage: A4 4%, A5 6%, B 10%, C 5% of A1-A3. Stage choices shift totals directly; the placeholders are not recommended once optional scope is included.

parameters.name: Industry Leadership Credits (ILC)
parameters.relationship: Appendix I: reporting credits (1-5% each) and reuse credits (relocate building 5%, salvage 1-5%, design for disassembly 1% per 2% of building), total max 5%, raise the limit factor to as much as 2.05.

parameters.name: Short-cycle biogenic carbon
parameters.relationship: Only short-cycle biogenic material (growth cycle of 10 years or less, waste, salvage, residues) may be deducted for compliance; other biogenic carbon, carbonation and Module D are reported separately, so long-rotation timber cannot offset the total.

parameters.name: Retained existing structure
parameters.relationship: NRC excludes reused portions from A-C but keeps their area in the denominator, while the baseline assumes all-new construction, so retention lowers EC_P against the baseline. HBP 2.1(f) bars demolishing a Class A heritage building.

parameters.name: GFA definition (GFA_NRC)
parameters.relationship: NRC GFA is fully enclosed area to the outside wall face, with no deduction for shafts or openings, excluding attached garages. It differs from zoning FSR area and Layer 0 GFA, so intensity needs its own field.

parameters.name: Transit-link scope and per-building reports
parameters.relationship: The below-grade transit link may or may not sit inside the object of assessment; default excludes public link structure beyond the lot (team assumption). GBPR needs one report per building, the Addendum one per parcel.

metrics.name: Embodied carbon vs intensity-path limit (headline)
metrics.good: Range upper bound <= 800 (ratio <= 2.0); up to 820 with maximum ILC
metrics.bad: Range upper bound > 800 fails this path; badge greyed unless quantities come from an imported BoM/IFC with EPDs
metrics.basis: VBBL 10.4.1.2 (official consolidation, S62) and Addendum v1.0 (S50): ECI 400, f = 2. Preset-based results are indicative ranges, not an ECDR; NRC says early-design results inform design only.
metrics.method: EC_P (A1-C4, substructure + shell, minus short-cycle biogenic) / GFA_NRC; range across preset bands

metrics.name: Embodied carbon vs baseline path
metrics.good: Report ratio design / baseline; limit 2.0 (plus ILC). Non-binding at f = 2 unless the design is less material-efficient than its baseline
metrics.bad: No pass signal at massing stage: ratio is about 1.0 by construction
metrics.basis: NRC s5.2 requires equivalent geometry and program; baseline uses industry-wide EPDs. Compute the baseline only from inputs that differ: parkade vs Addendum defaults, specified EPDs, retained structure, structural efficiency.
metrics.method: EC_P / EC_baseline; same tool, scope and 60-year period

metrics.name: GBPR on-track test vs limits expected at first Building Permit
metrics.good: Design inside the current limit and inside each expected-at-BP risk line (amber badges)
metrics.bad: Above an expected-at-BP line: forward risk, no formal pass/fail
metrics.basis: GBPR 3.1.1 and bulletin 4.1.1.1 (S01, S63) require the rezoning report to show the project is on track; the expected limits themselves are unadopted proposals.
metrics.method: Select regime lines by expected first-BP date; compare range with each line

metrics.name: Unadopted tightening (scenario lines only)
metrics.good: Scenario: <= 360 (380 with maximum ILC) or at least 10% below baseline; 2027 step TBD; 2030 baseline path -40%
metrics.bad: Above a scenario line: forward risk, no badge
metrics.basis: Sept 2024 staff deck (S52): 2025 proposal approved in principle, listed as delayed by the City (S54); 2027 and 2030 absolute values TBD. Not in 10.4.1.2.
metrics.method: Overlay dashed lines on the stacked bar; no pass/fail

metrics.name: 2030 proposal (baseline path -40%)
metrics.good: Design <= 0.6 x its functionally equivalent baseline (proposed); absolute path TBD. A 240 line (0.6 x 400) is team arithmetic, drawn dashed
metrics.bad: Bands: above 400 above benchmark; 240-400 between benchmark and team line; below 240 under team line
metrics.basis: Corrects '240 is the City's 2030 aspiration': the City proposal is baseline path -40% with absolute TBD (S52). The 40% is a city-wide CEAP target (S10).
metrics.method: Compare ratio to baseline with 0.6; optional comparison of intensity with 0.6 x 400

metrics.name: Indicative range vs MH 2023 high-rise archetype
metrics.good: Design range within MH 2023 25th to 50th percentile (179 to 260); range 97-424, baseline 311
metrics.basis: Numbers verified in S64 for a 30-storey residential archetype (A1-A5, B1-B4, C1-C4, 60 years, 20% SCM, window wall, 4-level parkade). Floor-area basis unconfirmed; transfer to a 244-305 m mixed-use tower is unverified.
metrics.method: Overlay the MH band on the stacked bar as context

modules.method: Massing-stage estimator, not a compliance tool or ECDR. 1) GFA_NRC excluding attached garages; parkade structure stays in the object. 2) Required scope: substructure and shell, including balconies, canopies and stairs. 3) Quantities = area x intensity preset by STRC system and height band (team assumption, with range) or user EPD entries (Reported GWP); no ICE data bundled. 4) A1-A3 plus A4-A5, B, C from entered data or placeholders (4/6/10/5% of A1-A3 only if a stage is missing). 5) Limit EC_L = 400 x GFA x (2 + ILC); baseline ratio only from inputs that differ. 6) Deduct short-cycle biogenic carbon; exclude retained structure from A-C. 7) Show current regime plus expected-at-BP lines for the first-BP date; Module D separate. 8) Report ranges; grey the badge unless BoM/IFC with EPDs.
visualization: Stacked bar by element and life-cycle stage with range whiskers, the 800 intensity line, dashed expected-at-BP lines and a dashed team 240 line
Baseline-path ratio dial labelled non-binding at f = 2
Waterfall of reduction levers (SCM, slab type, facade, parkade, procurement, retention) with MH and S59 magnitudes marked
MH 2023 range band (97-424, 179, 260, 311) as context
Badges linked to the clause; colour marks EPD-backed values vs presets; per-building tabs
modules.human_judgment: Defining the functionally equivalent baseline, structural material strategy, expected first-BP date, treatment of short-cycle biogenic carbon, selecting EPDs and reuse evidence, and judging whether a low-carbon structure is buildable at supertall height.
modules.limits: Massing-stage estimate with ranges; presets rest on a 30-storey archetype and a 2019 study, with no 244-305 m benchmark opened. The City requires listed tools (rezoning: One Click LCA Carbon Designer, Embodied Carbon Pathfinder, C.Scale) and its Design Report; this tool is none of them. Pathfinder is high-level and CC BY-NC-ND, so link only.

jury_criteria: design_excellence_20: sustainability, avoiding unnecessarily expensive or generic design

modules.name: Scoped carbon summary (structure + enclosure + operations; optional MEP and fit-out placeholders)
modules.design_question: Over a 60-year life, how do operational and embodied carbon compare within a stated scope, and which design lever cuts the total most?
inputs: P04-M03 annual energy by fuel and MFA
P04-M06 supply option and emission factors
P04-M05 PV generation and PV embodied carbon
P04-M07 embodied carbon by stage and GFA_NRC
Study period and B6 grid-factor scenario (compliance factor, BC 2025, or user path)
MFA/GFA_NRC ratio for denominator conversion
Optional placeholders: MEP (TM65-style kgCO2e/m2) and fit-out cycle length
outputs: Scoped carbon intensity (kgCO2e/m2 GFA_NRC) and total (tCO2e)
Operational vs embodied split under compliance and B6 factors
Lever ranking across modules
Board-ready carbon summary data for PRES, with scope stated

parameters.name: Study period
parameters.relationship: A longer period multiplies operational carbon (GHGI x years) but not embodied carbon; the City's guide fixes a 60-year lifespan for embodied-carbon studies.

parameters.name: Grid emission factor scenario (B6)
parameters.relationship: EMG 0.011 is a compliance factor. BC's consumption-based Integrated Grid factor was 9.9 t/GWh (2024) and 22.8 t/GWh (2025), about twice 0.011. Offer both plus a user decarbonisation path and state the scenario.

parameters.name: Supply mix (electric, gas, district)
parameters.relationship: Gas or district-steam share raises operational GHGI roughly in proportion to its factor times delivered energy (gas 0.180 vs electricity 0.011); set through P04-M06.

parameters.name: Refrigerant leakage (GHGI-R)
parameters.relationship: GHGI-R is reported outside the VBBL limit, so M08 adds it to operational carbon to keep it visible; over 60 years 0.2-2.6 kgCO2e/m2.yr is 12-156 kgCO2e/m2, so high-charge VRF matters.

parameters.name: Replacement cycles and service lives (B4)
parameters.relationship: Shorter component service lives raise stage B; the placeholder is 10% of A1-A3 when a tool lacks data. Fit-out cycle length is a team-assumed input.

parameters.name: MEP and fit-out scope
parameters.relationship: NRC makes services and interiors optional and points to TM65 and TM65LA for services. Office-heavy towers carry sizeable cyclic MEP and fit-out carbon, so scope changes the total. Placeholders are team assumptions; refrigerants stay in GHGI-R.

parameters.name: PV as operational credit and embodied debit
parameters.relationship: Show M05 PV both as an operational credit at the chosen grid factor and as an embodied debit, so shaded facade PV is not shown as carbon-negative by default.

parameters.name: Purchased renewable (RNG) accounting
parameters.relationship: EMG lets a lifetime-guaranteed renewable portion use factor zero for compliance. M08 adds a separate line at the physical factor so an accounting zero is not read as physical zero.

parameters.name: Biogenic carbon and carbonation
parameters.relationship: Only short-cycle biogenic carbon may be deducted for compliance (M07); other biogenic carbon and carbonation are shown separately and are not netted off the bar.

parameters.name: Denominator conversion (MFA vs GFA_NRC)
parameters.relationship: GHGI is per MFA; embodied carbon per GFA_NRC excl. attached garages. Scale operational carbon by rho = MFA/GFA_NRC (EMG expects MFA within 5% of drawing GFA) or report totals in tCO2e.

metrics.name: Scoped carbon intensity (illustrative; no pass/fail)
metrics.good: No threshold. With rho = 1 (+/-5% adds +/-9): at limits 800 + 3.0 x 60 = 980; at benchmark 400 + 180 = 580; at MH median 260 + 180 = 440; unadopted scenario 360 + 180 = 540.
metrics.basis: Arithmetic on sourced limits and MH 2023 median at the constant compliance factor, now with the MFA/GFA conversion stated. Scope excludes MEP and fit-out unless placeholders are added.
metrics.method: EC intensity + rho x sum over years of (GHGI + GHGI-R) at the chosen B6 factor

metrics.name: Operational share of scoped carbon (compliance vs B6 factor)
metrics.good: No threshold. All-electric at TEUI 100: GHGI 1.1 (0.011) vs 2.28 (0.0228); 60 years 66 vs 137 kgCO2e/m2. With embodied 260: 20% vs 35% operational; with 800: 8% vs 15%.
metrics.basis: Corrects 'operational carbon is small at 0.011': BC 2025 factor about twice (S65). Arithmetic with rho = 1; embodied 260 from S64 with unconfirmed area basis. Embodied likely still dominates.
metrics.method: Operational / (operational + embodied) under each factor

metrics.name: Embodied carbon vs 2030 proposal
metrics.good: Design <= 0.6 x equivalent baseline (proposed); absolute path TBD; 240 shown only as team arithmetic
metrics.basis: See P04-M07; the City proposal is baseline path -40% with absolute TBD (S52).
metrics.method: Compare with 0.6 x baseline from M07

modules.method: 1) Operational: annual GHGI per fuel from P04-M03 and P04-M06 times study years, under a stated B6 scenario (compliance 0.011, BC 2025 0.0228, or user path); recompute shares under both. 2) Add GHGI-R as a separate term and RNG at its physical factor as a separate line. 3) Show PV as operational credit and embodied debit (M05). 4) Embodied: A1-C4 intensity from M07, short-cycle biogenic deducted; Module D, other biogenic and carbonation separate. 5) Convert to one denominator (GFA_NRC) with rho = MFA/GFA_NRC, or show tCO2e. 6) Add optional MEP and fit-out placeholders (team assumptions). 7) Sum, no pass/fail; label scope on every chart. 8) Rank levers by kgCO2e/m2 saved; export numbers and source ids to PRES.
visualization: Stacked bar: embodied (A1-A5, B, C) plus operational over 60 years under compliance and B6 factors, with M01 and M07 limit markers and a scope label
Cumulative carbon timeline (year 0 to 60) showing embodied spike and operational ramp
Lever bar chart ranked by kgCO2e/m2 saved
Board-ready summary tile with source badges and denominators stated
modules.human_judgment: Study period and grid scenario, scope (MEP, fit-out), how to value biogenic carbon, trading operational against embodied carbon, and how to present the result for the jury.
modules.limits: Aggregates uncertain inputs; no sourced whole-life threshold. Grid factors beyond today are scenarios, not forecasts. Inherits M03/M07 limits. Scope is structure, enclosure and operations unless placeholders are added; do not compare with LETI or RIBA numbers. RICS WLCA second edition not opened.
