flags.claim: High-rise residential GHGI limit is 6 kgCO2e/m2.yr and hotel GHGI is 8 (2020-2023 tables, 2020 case study, ZEBX primer)
flags.correction: Under the 1 Mar 2025 wording and the 15 Sep 2025 VBBL, residential over 6 storeys is 3.0 and hotel 4.0 (Tables A and C). 6 and 8 applied Jul 2023 to Feb 2025.
flags.detail: Older values remain visible in the registry in FALSE ASSUMPTION colour. Verified r1 in S42, S43, S05; official consolidation S62 confirms.

flags.claim: The ICE database can be used freely for project embodied-carbon calculations in the tool
flags.correction: ICE Educational V5.0 is educational-only; non-educational use is not permitted after 30 Sep 2026 and it cannot be used in tools or reporting.
flags.detail: Do not bundle or query ICE in the hosted tool at all; accept only user-typed factors with the user's licence attestation. Use EC3 data (account, attribution, limits) or user values.

flags.claim: Vancouver requires new towers to cut embodied carbon by 40%
flags.correction: The 40% is a city-wide 2030 target in the Climate Emergency Action Plan. The by-law limit is 2 x a benchmark (VBBL 10.4.1.2); the proposed 2025 reductions are delayed.
flags.detail: The tool shows the 40% line as an aspiration only; r2 shows the 2030 proposal as baseline path -40% with absolute TBD.

flags.claim: Tower dwellings can rely on passive cooling if overheating stays under 200 hours
flags.correction: BCBC 2024 (in VBBL 2025) requires at least one cool space at or below 26 deg C in every dwelling, so passive-only dwellings are not allowed.
flags.detail: EMG v3.0 requires passive overheating hours to be reported with cooling disabled; the final EMG sets no hour limit (r2), so 200 h is a team assumption.

flags.claim: By-law 13472 limits (office 25, retail 14 kgCO2e/m2.yr) govern a new tower's permit
flags.correction: They apply to existing office and retail buildings of 9,290 m2 or more from 2026; new towers are governed by VBBL Part 10 and the rezoning policy.
flags.detail: Reference Manual opened r2 (S18). Used only as a forward-looking risk indicator (2040 limit GHGI 0, heat intensity 0.09 GJ/m2.yr from S02); enforcement may be paused (May 2026 motion).

flags.claim: Current energy rule for cultural/civic ('all other') space is the 2018-20 rule (TEUI 35% better than baseline, TEDI and GHGI equal to baseline)
flags.correction: Table A (from Jul 2023, unchanged in Mar and Sep 2025): GHGI limit is 50% below a fossil-fuel-only reference model; TEUI/TEDI follow the NECB 2020 / ASHRAE 90.1-2019 reference model (EMG s5.1-5.3).
flags.detail: The 35% saving came from the 2017/2018 rezoning policy. Superseded for current permits; kept visible as FALSE ASSUMPTION. HBP has no row for these groups.

flags.claim: Assembly, care and industrial (Group A, B, F) GHGI must be 85% below a fossil-fuel-only reference from Jan 2025 (City 2022 deck; round-1 critique)
flags.correction: The adopted VBBL Table A (Mar 2025, Sep 2025, official consolidation) says 50% lower; EMG s5.3 example also uses 0.50.
flags.detail: The 85% step was approved in principle in 2022 but is not in the by-law text opened; the critique correction was itself corrected against primary text.

flags.claim: In a mixed-use building only the residential portion must separately meet its own TEDI limit
flags.correction: All portions with a table TEDI target must meet their combined TEDI target, and portions with an absolute GHGI target their combined GHGI target, in addition to whole-building limits (EMG s5.1(e)).
flags.detail: Confirmed in the final EMG text (r2). The residential-only check in the eSim case arose because residential was the only portion with a TEDI target there.

flags.claim: Embodied carbon above 800 kgCO2e/m2 fails in any case
flags.correction: 800 (2 x 400 x GFA) is the intensity-path limit only. The baseline path allows up to 2 x a functionally equivalent baseline, which can exceed 800 for a supertall.
flags.detail: Also, 800 was the Oct 2023 cap; the current by-law uses factor f = 2 on either benchmark. r2 adds that the baseline path is non-binding at massing stage.

flags.claim: The 2025 embodied-carbon limits (360/320 absolute; 10% or 20% reduction plus responsible-materials option) are in force and 'verified'
flags.correction: VBBL 10.4.1.2 (15 Sep 2025) and Addendum v1.0 set f = 2 (limit = 2 x benchmark). The 2025 reductions were proposed, then listed by the City as delayed; next update TBD.
flags.detail: The tool shows 360 / -10% only as an unadopted scenario with no pass/fail. Sources: S49, S50, S52, S54, S62.

flags.claim: The 2021-table TEUI/TEDI values and the Jan 2025 GHGI step were 'verified' from a consultant page and a 2022 deck
flags.correction: Values are now verified in the City's wordings: GHGI steps took effect in the 1 Mar 2025 wording (not January 2025); TEUI/TEDI cells unchanged since Jan 2022.
flags.detail: The label was premature in the first draft; fixed by opening S42-S44, S49 and, in r2, the official consolidation S62.

flags.claim: GHGI-R (refrigerant leakage) counts inside the GHGI limit from January 2025
flags.correction: EMG v3.0 defines GHGI-R as a separate metric with no compliance requirement; Table A GHGI covers energy only.
flags.detail: The City planned inclusion from Jan 2025 (Focal report background), but v3.0 adopted separate reporting; final EMG Eq. 3 opened r2.

flags.claim: The City halved the TEDI/TEUI corridor-pressurization credit (complete description of the change)
flags.correction: Superseded in r2: the final EMG v3.0 keeps the corridor TEDI adjustment maximum at 10 (minimum 0), TEUI adjustment equal to TEDI adjustment, and shows no GHGI adjustment. Focal's 5 was a recommendation.
flags.detail: The r1 correction (max 5, GHGI adjustment removed) came from the Focal report and the redline; the final text (S17) does not adopt the 5.

flags.claim: District steam connection qualifies as an LCES and earns Table C relief
flags.correction: Only conditionally: the 2021 City letter recognises planned electrode boilers if built as planned, not for permits before approvals and construction start, and with written utility confirmation. Under the LCES Policy it is a Type 4 route with extra conditions.
flags.detail: Plant status in 2026 not found. Table C relief is VBBL-only and locked until the user attests a City recognition document; HBP targets are stricter.

flags.claim: Active cooling is required in every room of every dwelling (26 deg C, windows closed) from 1 Jan 2025
flags.correction: BCBC 2024, adopted in VBBL 2025, requires at least one cool space at or below 26 deg C per dwelling at summer design temperature.
flags.detail: Earlier City deck and Focal report wording was broader; the by-law clause itself was not located in Division B text.

flags.claim: Pool and amenity space raises TEDI sharply (58% of heating from pools)
flags.correction: Under EMG v3.0 definitions pool-water heating, DHW and humidification are excluded from TEDI; they count in TEUI and GHGI. Pool-hall conditioning and ventilation heating still count in TEDI.
flags.detail: The 58% figure is a 2018-20 case under older rules; the final EMG TEDI definition confirms the exclusions.

flags.claim: Biogenic carbon is excluded from compliance, so timber storage cannot offset the compliance total
flags.correction: Short-cycle biogenic carbon (growth cycle 10 years or less, waste, salvage, residues) may be deducted for compliance; other biogenic carbon, carbonation and Module D are reported separately.
flags.detail: Addendum v1.0 s4.4(a). Long-rotation timber does not qualify.

flags.claim: VBBL Table A (or Table C with an LCES) sets the energy targets for a VTC tower, and the Higher Buildings Policy's sustainability expectations are unknown
flags.correction: HBP s2.2 (amended 31 Mar 2026) requires Passive House, or TEUI/TEDI/GHGI targets (residential 100/15/3, hotel 120/15/4, retail and office 100/15/1.5) AND LCES connection with no aggregation; the GBPR also applies.
flags.detail: HBP opened r2 (S60). Targets are stricter than Table A (TEDI 15 everywhere; GHGI 1.5 retail and office); Table C relief does not apply. Basis (MFA, EMG) and mixed-use weighting are not stated.

flags.claim: The Sustainable Large Developments policy requires a low-carbon energy supply feasibility study that M06 should feed as a rezoning deliverable
flags.correction: SLD (amended 31 Mar 2026; sites of 8,000 m2 or more, or 45,000 m2 of new floor area) has sections A-G: site design, food assets, green mobility, potable water, groundwater, zero waste, affordable housing. It has no energy section or energy study.
flags.detail: Opened r2 (S61). The VTC block (about 11,470 m2) triggers SLD. The r1 claim came from the critic's memory. Requirements route to PROG, ECOL and MOBI.

flags.claim: Whether on-site PV lowers GHGI under EMG v3.0 is unresolved
flags.correction: Final EMG Eq. 2 subtracts site renewable generation before applying the emission factor, so PV lowers GHGI at 0.011 kgCO2e/kWh as well as TEUI.
flags.detail: S17 opened r2. The effect is small on a low-carbon grid. The 7% reduced-factor rule from v2.0 is not in the final text.

flags.claim: Whether an all-electric heat-pump plant counts as an on-site LCES is unresolved
flags.correction: LCES Policy Type 3 sets criteria: seasonal average COP > 2, modelled GHGI < limit minus 33%, gas peaking sized to augment, 2-year and 5-year contracts, and an engineer's written verification.
flags.detail: S41 opened r2. A heat pump is not automatically an LCES; it must meet Type 3 and the City decides recognition.

flags.claim: BC electricity at 0.011 kgCO2e/kWh means operational carbon is small, so embodied carbon dominates whole-life carbon (M08)
flags.correction: 0.011 is the EMG compliance factor. BC's consumption-based Integrated Grid factor was 9.9 t/GWh (2024) and 22.8 t/GWh (2025), about twice 0.011; embodied carbon likely still dominates, but by less.
flags.detail: S65 opened r2 (updated 26 May 2026; net-import years 2023-24). M08 separates the compliance factor from the B6 scenario.

flags.claim: The City's 2030 embodied-carbon aspiration is 240 kgCO2e/m2 (0.6 x 400)
flags.correction: The City proposal (S52) lists 2030 as baseline path -40% with the absolute path TBD; 240 is team arithmetic and appears only as a labelled dashed line.
flags.detail: M07 and M08 show 2030 as -40% vs equivalent baseline and define a continuous band around the benchmark and the team line.

flags.claim: A massing-stage design passing the baseline path (<= 2 x baseline) is a meaningful compliance signal
flags.correction: NRC s5.2 requires equivalent geometry and program, so a preset-built design equals its own baseline (ratio about 1.0). At f = 2 the baseline path is non-binding; the intensity path and expected-at-BP lines carry the test.
flags.detail: M07 shows the baseline ratio with a non-binding note and computes the baseline only from inputs that differ (parkade, EPDs, retention, efficiency).

flags.claim: EMG v3.0 cuts the corridor TEDI/TEUI adjustment maximum from 10 to 5 and removes the GHGI adjustment (the r1 correction)
flags.correction: Final EMG v3.0 s2.5.2 keeps the TEDI adjustment maximum at 10 (minimum 0), sets the TEUI adjustment equal to it, and shows no GHGI adjustment. Focal's 5 was a recommendation that the final text did not adopt.
flags.detail: S17 opened r2; the r1 statement rested on the Focal report and the redline. M02 and M01 now cite max 10.

flags.claim: HBP Figure 1 (areas where higher buildings are permitted), the HBP modelling basis (MFA, EMG, mixed-use weighting) and the City's LCES recognition letters
flags.detail: HBP text opened r2, but Figure 1 is not text-extractable and s2.2 does not name the modelling basis. Area-weighting HBP targets by MFA follows EMG s5.1 by analogy.

flags.claim: Creative Energy's electrode boilers are commissioned and have spare capacity for the VTC site, and the LCES Type 4 route is still open
flags.detail: City letter (2021) confirms at least 10 MW planned; 2021 announcements anticipated 2024 commissioning; no 2026 status or steam emission factor found. The LCES Policy says the City may close Type 4.

flags.claim: BC Hydro can serve a tower of roughly 100,000 m2 at the site without delay
flags.detail: No public capacity data. Dal Grauer is being replaced by West End (as early as 2032), Murrin by East Vancouver (2031). Electrical By-law 5563 opened r2 (no capacity rule); BC Hydro large-load process unopened.

flags.claim: Energize Vancouver (By-law 13472) enforcement is paused
flags.detail: A 20 May 2026 Council Members' motion proposes it; the City page confirms only a review of VBBL, Energize Vancouver and Energy Step Code alignment (report-back 2027).

flags.claim: The +10% floor-space incentive for larger buildings meeting ILFI Zero Energy or Passive House applies to a CD-1 tower rezoning
flags.detail: City page lists it to 31 Oct 2030 and says to apply through a development or combined permit with the bulletin section 3 material; the zoning mechanism for a CD-1 rezoning was not opened.

flags.claim: PV life-cycle carbon per kWp, and that facade PV can raise whole-life carbon on BC's grid
flags.detail: IEA PVPS 2020 (S66) gives inventories and Canadian yields, but per-kWh GHG results were not extracted. The critic's 'several times the grid factor' is unconfirmed; the tool uses EPD inputs and arithmetic payback.

flags.claim: MH 2023 intensities (97-424, median 260, baseline 311) as anchors for a 244-305 m mixed-use tower
flags.detail: S64 numbers verified for a 30-storey residential archetype; the floor-area basis is unconfirmed and no tall-building benchmark (CTBUH, CLF, Foraboschi 2014) was opened. The height premium stays a team assumption.

flags.claim: EC3 terms permit caching or redistributing EPD values to other users of an open-source hosted tool
flags.detail: Only rate limits, attribution and paid commercial tier were read (S29). Check redistribution clauses before any hosted query; Pathfinder is CC BY-NC-ND, so link only.

flags.claim: HBP s2.1(c) places the highest CBD buildings at about 550-700 ft; VTC towers of 244-305 m are about 800-1,000 ft
flags.detail: Cross-packet flag to SITE and PROG. HBP is under review (S37) and the VTC site is hypothetical; s2.1(f) bars demolishing a Class A heritage building, which constrains the M07 retention lever.

flags.claim: Where the real SLD requirements land in the platform
flags.detail: Cross-packet routing: parks, trees and soil, food assets, TDM and EV, water balance, groundwater, zero waste and 20% social plus 10% rental housing go to PROG, ECOL and MOBI. SLD A.3.3 setbacks and E.3.1 affect M07 parkade.

flags.claim: Higher Buildings Policy Review may change the s2.2 energy requirements for towers
flags.detail: The policy already has targets (S60); Phase I ran Apr-May 2026 and policy approaches are shared in early 2027, so limits may change after the competition.

flags.claim: VBBL energy limits and Energize Vancouver may change after the 21 May 2026 Council review
flags.detail: Staff report back in 2027; the by-law is unchanged meanwhile. Limits shown are as of 15 Sep 2025 wording and may not match a later permit.

flags.claim: WWR preset of 40% as the good/bad line
flags.detail: 40% is the sourced reference-building cap on the NECB path (VBBL 10.2.2.3); using it as a design target is a team choice. Editable.

flags.claim: Peak electrical demand densities (electrified-load presets), PV viability cut-offs and PV share targets
flags.detail: No Vancouver-sourced values found; all are editable presets or user inputs.

flags.claim: Embodied-carbon 240 kgCO2e/m2 team line and whole-life illustrative sums of 980, 580, 540 and 440 kgCO2e/m2
flags.detail: Arithmetic on sourced numbers (0.6 x 400; 800 + 3.0 x 60; 400 + 180; 360 + 180; 260 + 180); not regulatory values and shown without pass/fail.

flags.claim: TEDI proxy, thermal-bridging presets and structural intensity presets with ranges
flags.detail: Proxy is uncalibrated (band, greyed badge); BETBG psi values and supertall quantity presets are unopened and labelled team assumption until benchmarked.

flags.claim: HBP weighting by MFA for mixed uses, a VBBL reference-model proxy for Groups A, B, F, and applying the Type 3 'limit minus 33%' to the HBP target
flags.detail: HBP has no mixed-use or Group A/B/F rule; EMG s5.1 and Table A are used by analogy. All three are editable toggles in M01 and M06.

flags.claim: Expected first Building Permit date of 2028 or later, passive overheating presets (200 h, 20 h), height premium above 40 storeys, PV payback cut-off, and MEP and fit-out placeholders
flags.detail: No sourced values: the BP date is the critic's estimate, the overheating presets are not in the final EMG, and the others are editable presets shown with ranges.
